**Feature Extraction:** Pass both images through a pre-trained convolutional neural network to extract multi-scale feature maps.
**Per-Patch Comparison:** Compute the normalized Euclidean distance between the feature vectors of $I_{ref}$ and $I_{pred}$ at each spatial location and channel.
**Aggregation:** Average the distances across all spatial locations and channels to produce a single scalar LPIPS score.
- $f_{l,c}(i,j)$ is the feature value at layer $l$, channel $c$, position $(i,j)$.
- Ensure consistent normalization between reference and prediction images to avoid biased distances.
- Degenerate inputs (e.g., constant color images) may yield non-zero LPIPS due to feature space variance.
LPIPS is computationally more expensive than PSNR or SSIM due to the need for feature extraction via a deep neural network.
It provides a better correlation with human perception than pixel-based metrics.
It is suitable for evaluating perceptual quality in radiance field optimization where structural fidelity is critical.
LPIPS was introduced as a learned perceptual image patch similarity metric.
